Take this with a pinch of salt as I'm new around here. I've always believed the MPL to be the lower limit of the FO zone when price changed direction.

So there will be outstanding orders at that price and it will be the last place for price to turn when it comes back to that area. It sometimes turns below the MPL, but to get the best price you wait for it to reach the MPL. It doesn't always happen, so you get fewer trades that way. The trades you do get will have a higher R.

Edge

The MPL will always be the last set of orders. This can be right down to the tick. Lower scales in a flag will show you where the smallest order blocks may reside to cause the maximum pain.

1373

What you have drawn are caps. An MPL is the maximum pain level which the IT can give to retailers before turning price. As Edge said, the last set of orders inside a flag. Look at in terms of fractals. Draw flags on the TF you wish to trade then dig down to the lowest tf you can go and find the last set of orders inside that area you wish to trade. An easy way to start understanding how it works is draw Flags on the lowest timeframe inside the larger flag which you are looking to trade and you will find pockets of unfilled orders ready to be taken. the last set of such orders is the MPL.
